**Finding: compliant** (Rule ASSIGN, § 14.1, paragraph p0121).

- **Customer assignment on M&A:** Section 14.1 lets either party — including Corio — assign without consent in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets related to the Agreement. The required successor carve-out is present, so the walk-away scenario (blanket prohibition, no M&A carve-out) does not arise.
- **Change of control:** No "change of control" or "deemed an assignment" language appears anywhere in the document, and § 11.2 / § 11.3 give Commerce One no termination or re-pricing right on a change of control of Corio.
- **Position reached:** At the fallback and largely at preferred — mutual successor assignment right, with no notice condition even imposed on us.
- **Noted, not flagged:** no express affiliate carve-out, and consent for other assignments is not qualified as "not to be unreasonably withheld." The direct-competitor consent proviso is reciprocal and mirrors the protection our own playbook seeks against vendor assignments. These are minor gaps against preferred wording, so no redline was proposed.
